What to Expect from a Tranexamic, Alpha Arbutin & Azelaic Acid

 

It can be challenging to determine whether a dark spot remover will work because not every dark spot is the same. There’s no such thing as a universal solution, which is why you may have to do a little trial and error with products formulated with the ingredients mentioned above. 

  • Darkness from acne spots or dyspigmentation (an abnormality in the formation or distribution of pigmentation in the skin) tends to respond well to over-the-counter dark spot remedies. Keep in mind that it can take up to three months to start to see results. 
  • Age or sunspots, as well as freckles, are caused by sun exposure. While there’s no harm in trying the best age spot remover, discoloration caused by the sun may have a better response to a prescription cream or dermatological treatment such as laser resurfacing. 
  • Even after you’ve chosen one of the best products for dark spots, don’t forget to wear a broad spectrum UVA/UVB sunscreen with a minimum SPF of 30 every day. Sunscreen will help prevent current spots from becoming dark while helping to prevent new ones from forming.

FAQs

What causes dark spots?

Dark spots result from hyperpigmentation due to acne scarring or spending too much time in the sun. Other causes include hormonal issues, liver damage, genetics, and various skin disorders.

Where do dark spots occur?

Dark spots can occur anywhere on the body, though they’re mostly found on the cheeks, forehead, and upper lip, or around the mouth. They can also appear on the neck, hands, and legs. But keep in mind: dark spots can pretty much pop up anywhere, especially areas of your body that are more often exposed to the sun.

What do dermatologists recommend for dark spots?

Dermatologists typically recommend laser treatments, chemical peels, cryotherapy, microdermabrasion, or a prescription cream — all of which lessen the appearance of dark spots faster than topical products.

Why won’t my dark spots fade?

You may be doing too much to fade stubborn spots. Suppose you’re using overly harsh products such as astringents or non-skin-safe spot correctors — or are trying to “scrub” marks away with an exfoliator. In that case, you can actually worsen the pigmentation. The skin can become darker and rougher in texture.

Is retinol or vitamin C better for dark spots?

Both are incredibly effective. Vitamin C brightens and improves pigmentation issues, while retinol stimulates collagen production, another way to remove dark spots. You have to be careful not to use retinol that’s too strong for your skin because it can cause inflammation and exacerbate dark spots. You can find some dark spot serums that are safely formulated to include both active ingredients, which is a win-win.

Those with darker skin tones may have a higher risk of discoloration or hyperpigmentation from the use of retinol, so this ingredient (along with prescription-strength ingredients) should be used sparingly.

How do I apply the best dark spot correctors?

There isn’t one answer to this question because it depends on the formula, strength, and size of the area(s) you’re treating. Generally, prescription-strength creams are applied only to areas of concern a few times a week. For the most part, OTC correctors such as those on our list can be applied daily and all over the face — but be sure to read the instructions on the package first. Don’t forget the sunscreen during the day.

How can I remove dark spots on my skin naturally?

While you shouldn’t expect any miracles, some DIY home remedies may have a subtle effect on dark spots — for example, a lemon juice and yogurt face mask. Or, you could also apply the following topically: buttermilk, aloe, tomatoes, and papaya.

What color neutralizes dark spots?

If you’re looking to cover up dark spots with a concealer temporarily, peachy and orange-hued shades are generally best for counteracting the look of darkness and brightening dark spots. A color corrector for dark spots works according to the principles of the color wheel — the opposite of one another on the color wheel can cancel the other out.

Sources:
“Quantifying Dyspigmentation in Facial Skin ageing: an Explorative Study,” US National Library of Medicine National Center for Biology.
